title: A1-08 · Prepositions and expression of having a

blocks.text: A1-08 · Prepositions and expression of having a
Lesson overview

Arabic does not have a verb "to have" . To say "I have a machine" says "I have a machine": ⁧عِنْدِي⁩ . ⁧سَيَّارَةٌ⁩ This unit gives you the prepositions to place people and objects in space (above, below, in front, next to) and the three buildings of possession with ⁧عِنْدَ⁩ , ⁧لِـ⁩ and ⁧مَعَ⁩ . You will also learn that after a preposition the name changes the final vowel: it is the first grammatical case you consciously use. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 23–24 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-08), voice synthesis script, a plan of your room designed by hand, session with the tutor in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. use the most frequent site prepositions and tell where objects and people are located;
2. put the name to the genitive after a preposition ( ⁧فِي البَيْتِ، فِي بَيْتٍ كَبِيرٍ⁩ );
3. attach singular suffix pronouns to prepositions ( ⁧عِنْدِي، مَعَكَ، لَهَا، فِيهِ⁩ );
4. express possession with ⁧عِنْدَ⁩ , ⁧لِـ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ⁩ and deny it with ⁧لَيْسَ عِنْدِي⁩ ;
5. give simple directions in the city without verbs;
6. describe a room and write what you possess in 40 words.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: 1. Dialogue 1 · Where is the key?
In the office, Luca looks for the key to the archive.

rows: Luke: Where is the key, Karīm?
Karīm: On the desk, next to the computer.
Lūkā: lā, ʿalā l-maktabi awrāqun faqaṭ.
No, there's only paper on the desk.
Karīm: Is the key in the bag?
Lūkā: al-ḥaqībatu taḥta ṭ-ṭāwila, wa- fīhā ǧawāzu safarī wa-hātifī faqaṭ.
Luca: The bag is under the table, and inside there are only my passport and my phone.
Karīm: āh, āsif! al-miftāḥu maʿī, fī ǧaybī!
Karīm: Sorry! I have the key in my pocket!

blocks.text: ! ⁧الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: al-ḥamdu li-llāh! Luca: Thank God!

What to notice. After each preposition the name ends in -i: ⁧عَلَى المَكْتَبِ⁩ , ⁧بِجَانِبِ الحَاسُوبِ⁩ , ⁧تَحْتَ فِيهَا⁩ . ⁧الطَّاوِلَةِ⁩ It shall be ⁧فِي⁩ with the suffix -hā (The bag is feminine). ⁧مَعِي⁩ With me, he expresses what is on him at that moment. ⁧الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ⁩ here it's worth less bad.
2. Prepositions of place

rows: ⁧أَمَامَ البَابِ⁩ In front of the door
⁧بَيْنَ البَنْكِ وَالمَطْعَمِ⁩ The bank and the restaurant are located between the bank and the restaurant

blocks.text: ⁧عَنْ⁩ ʿan regarding, on; from (far from) ⁧عَنِ المَدِينَةِ⁩ The city is under attack. ⁧لِـ⁩ and ⁧بِـ⁩ , as ⁧وَ⁩ ( L0-10): ⁧لِلطَّالِبِ⁩ , ⁧بِالسَّيَّارَةِ⁩ . With the article ⁧لِـ⁩ loses the alif: . ⁧لِلْ⁩ Preposition-name. ⁧فَوْقَ⁩ , ⁧تَحْتَ⁩ , ⁧أَمَامَ⁩ , ⁧خَلْفَ⁩ , ⁧بَيْنَ⁩ , ⁧عِنْدَ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ⁩ They end up in -a: originally they are names to the accusative used as place adverbs. For this reason the name that follows you is a complement of specification, to the genitive, as in aiḍāfa (A1-10).
3. The genitive after the preposition
After any preposition the name is at the genitive ( ⁧مَجْرُور⁩ maǧrūr , "Draged"): desinence becomes -i if the name is determined, -indeterminate. The adjective that follows it agrees also in case.
⁧فِي بَغْدَادَ، مِنْ مِصْرَبَغْدَادُ، مِصْرُ⁩ fī Baġdādmin Miṣr

The diptotic names (many proper names, some plurals) to the indeterminate genitive take -a, without tanwīn: ⁧فِي بَغْدَادَ⁩ , ⁧مِنْ لُبْنَانَ⁩ , ⁧مِنْ أَطِبَّاءَ⁩ . You've met them before: now you know why. In pause desinence falls, as always: fī I-bayt. But inside the sentence it must be read, and in the vocally written texts you see it written: it is proof that a name depends on a preposition. Because you need it. In the news the additions introduced by preposition are everywhere ( ⁧فِي العَاصِمَةِ، عَلَى الحُدُودِ، مِنَ الحُكُومَةِ⁩ ). Recognizing the -i immediately tells you that word is not the subject.
4. The prepositions with the suffixes
Prepositions take suffix pronouns (which you will see on the names in A1-09):

Three rules. 1) ⁧لِـ⁩ becomes ⁧لَـ⁩ in front of the suffixes ( ⁧لَكَ⁩ , ⁧لَهُ⁩ ), except for: ⁧لِي⁩ . 2) -hu becomes -hi after i, ī or ay: ⁧فِيهِ⁩ , ⁧عَلَيْهِ⁩ (and in A1-09 ⁧بَيْتِهِ⁩ to the genitive). 3) ⁧عَلَى⁩ and ⁧إِلَى⁩ change the alif maqṣūra in ay: ⁧عَلَيْكَ⁩ , ⁧إِلَيْهِ⁩ . Recognize ⁧عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ of A1-01: è ⁧عَلَى⁩ + -kum ... on you.
5. •Having: three constructions

rows: I have a car. · He has a meeting.
I have a brother in Cairo.

blocks.text: ⁧مَعَ⁩ + possess what you have with you now. ⁧مَعِي جَوَازُ سَفَرِي⁩ I've got my passport.

How the sentence works. ⁧عِنْدِي سَيَّارَةٌ⁩ It is a nominal phrase with the predicate in the head: "A self-stressed one." What is possessed is the subject, indefinite and to the name (-one), just as in ⁧فِي الشَّارِعِ سَيَّارَةٌ⁩ ( A1-04). With a holder expressed by a name: ⁧عِنْدَ سَلْمَى سَيَّارَةٌ⁩ « Salmā He's got a car. Question. ⁧هَلْ عِنْدَكَ وَقْتٌ؟⁩ Do you have time? ⁧هَلْ مَعَكِ قَلَمٌ؟⁩ Do you have a pen (with you)? A1-16). Putting on ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ front: ⁧لَيْسَ عِنْدِي سَيَّارَةٌ⁩ I don't have a car. ⁧لَيْسَ مَعِي مِفْتَاحٌ⁩ I don't have the key with me. The rest doesn't change. In A1-16 You'll see. ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ in all its forms.
6. Dialogue 2 · To the market
Salmā buy bread at an Arab grocery store in Milan.

rows: Salmā: as-salāmu ʿalaykum. hal ʿindaka ḫubzun ʿarabī?
SalmāMorning. Do you have any Arabic bread?
al-bāʾiʿ: wa-ʿalaykumu s-salām. naʿam, ʿindī ḫubzun ǧadīd. tafaḍḍalī.
Good morning. Yeah, I got fresh bread. Please.
Salmā: Thank you. Do you have any mint?
al-bāʾiʿ: lā, āsif, laysa ʿindī naʿnāʿuni l- yawm.
The seller: No, I'm sorry, I have no mint today.
Salmā: So where do I find mint? (Lett. Where's the mint then?)
⁧عِنْدَ البَائِعِ المَغْرِبِيِّ، فِي⁩ : ⁧البَائِعُ⁩ . ⁧السُّوقِ، بَيْنَ المَقْهَى وَالبَنْكِ⁩
al-bāʾiʿ: ʿinda l-bāʾiʿi l-maġribiyyi, fī s-sūqi, bayna l-maqhā wa-l-bank.
The seller: From the Moroccan seller, to the market, between the coffee and the bank.
Salmā: Is the market far away?
al-bāʾiʿ: lā, huwa qarībun ǧiddan, amāma l-maḥaṭṭa.
The seller: No, it's very close, in front of the station.

blocks.text: ⁧مَعَ⁩ . ⁧شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: šukran ǧazīlan. maʿa s-salāma. Salmā: Thank you very much. Goodbye.
. ⁧السَّلَامَةِ⁩

What to notice. Salmā gives the seller a "tu" ( ⁧عِنْدَكَ⁩ ): In standard Arabic it is normal. ⁧المَقْهَى⁩ The coffee (local) is in alif maqṣūra And it doesn't change to the genitive. ⁧السُّوق⁩ is male or female depending on use: here male ( ⁧بَعِيدٌ⁩ ).
7. Directions in town, no verbs
For now describe the location of the places; the movement verbs ('gira', 'go straight') will arrive in A2.

rows: The station is on the right.
The bank is left, next to the restaurant.
The museum is in front of you.
The pharmacy is after the mosque.
markazu š-šurṭati bayna l-banki wa-l- madrasa.
The police station is between the bank and the school.
The market is close to here.

blocks.text: 8. Pronunciation

ʿayn in the prepositions. ⁧عَلَى⁩ , ⁧عِنْدَ⁩ , ⁧عَنْ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ⁩ : four very frequent words with ʿayn. alā , Inda are the typical mistakes. The ā of ⁧عَلَى⁩ and ⁧إِلَى⁩ before the article. It is written long but it reads short, because they follow two consonants: ʿala l-maktab , ila l-maḥaṭṭa . In the transliteration of the volume we write it long for fidelity to the graph; Reading, abbreviating. The genitive in the chain. fī l-bayti l-kabīr : the name -i ties with the adjective article. Exercise with the sentences of the section 3 until she comes out without thinking about it. The šadda of ⁧عَلَيَّ⁩ and ⁧فِيَّ⁩ . ʿalayya , fiyya: the double y is heard. The grouping. ⁧بِجَانِبِ⁩ It reads like a word: bi-ǧānibi .
9. New lexicon
⁧مَجْرُور⁩ maǧrūr (name) to the parent ⁧ج ر ر⁩ word

Notes of use. In many countries, bank is also used ⁧مَصْرِف⁩ maṣrif (official and banking language). ⁧مَقْهًى⁩ in the plural and without article it has the form of a "defective" with tanwīn -an/-in: you will study it in B1; with the article is simply ⁧المَقْهَى⁩ . ⁧أَخ⁩ with the suffixes has particular forms ( ⁧أَخِي⁩ My brother... ⁧أَخُوكَ⁩ Your brother: A1-09. ⁧وَقْت⁩ It is the time you have or do not have; The atmospheric weather is ⁧الجَوّ⁩ or ⁧الطَّقْس⁩ .
